Article Title: IISc develops 3D-printed model to study how cancer drugs penetrate tumours
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Researchers from IISc have developed a low-cost, 3D-printed device that could help scientists understand why cancer drugs are less effective in deeper regions of solid tumours.The device recreates the nutrient- and oxygen-deprived conditions found inside tumours and allows researchers to examine how cancer cells respond to drugs at different depths.The platform, developed by researchers from IISc’s Department of Chemical Engineering, addresses a longstanding challenge in cancer research: reproducing the complex microenvironment of solid tumours in laboratory conditions while retaining access to cells from different regions for analysis.In solid tumours, blood vessels are often poorly developed and unevenly distributed.Consequently, cells closer to blood vessels receive more oxygen and nutrients, while those farther away experience shortages. These differences can influence how cancer cells grow and respond to treatment.Conventional laboratory methods that grow cancer cells in flat, two-dimensional layers do not adequately reproduce these conditions.One approach to overcoming this limitation is the 'Cells-in-Gel-in-Paper' (CiGiP) model, in which cancer cells embedded in a gel are grown on stacked paper layers.Nutrients and oxygen supplied from one side diffuse through the stack, creating conditions resembling different depths of a tumour. However, existing versions of this technique rely on wax-printed or hydrophobic barriers to contain the cell culture within each paper layer. The discontinuation of solid-ink printers, which were used for this purpose, has made the method less accessible to laboratories.The IISc team has replaced this requirement with a simple press-fit enclosure made using fused deposition modelling (FDM) 3D printers. Designed by Ankit Kumar, a PhD student in the laboratory of Bhushan J Toley, the device holds eight circular paper discs together through gentle, uniform pressure, preventing nutrients and drugs from leaking around their edges. Culture medium is supplied through an inlet at the top.The researchers tested the platform using MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells embedded in Matrigel. After 72 hours, they found that the number of live cells progressively decreased from the topmost to the bottommost layer, while dead cells increased. Expression of HIF-1alpha, a gene associated with low-oxygen conditions, also rose towards the deeper layers, confirming that the model recreated a hypoxic tumour-like environment.The team then examined how the chemotherapy drug doxorubicin penetrated the tissue. Drug uptake declined progressively across the eight layers, indicating that deeper regions received less of the drug. Longer treatment periods partially overcame these diffusion limitations.The researchers also tested doxorubicin and paclitaxel, individually and in combination.Using a statistical method called the Bliss synergy score, they found that the two drugs had an antagonistic interaction across all eight layers when administered together. This means their combined effect was lower than what would be expected if the drugs acted independently.Published in Analytical Methods in 2026, the study was led by Toley, with Kumar and Shweta Kumar as co-authors. The researchers have made the device’s design files publicly available to facilitate reproduction.They believe the approach could make paper-supported 3D tumour models more accessible for drug screening and studies of treatment response.
Article Summary: Device recreates nutrient- and oxygen-deprived conditions found inside tumours. Allows researchers to examine how cancer cells respond to drugs at different depths. Could help scientists understand why cancer drugs are less effective in deeper regions of solid tumour.

Article Title: AI may improve patient discharge summaries, study shows
Article Text:
AI-Generated Image

npj Digital Medicine,

The use of artificial intelligence (AI) could help physicians prepare hospital patient discharge summaries more efficiently and with greater accuracy and completeness, according to a study.Discharge summaries provide essential information for patients when they leave a hospital. The data includes essential information such as a patient's treatment, medication needs, changes in medication, unresolved medical issues and follow-up needs as an outpatient. Primary care physicians rely on discharge summaries to continue their care of patients, and discharge summaries help to provide a patient care roadmap going forward.This study, published in the journalfocused on longer, complex hospital stays, where there is a larger volume of medical information to summarize. Such in-house scenarios can be a significant burden for providers and add to their time spent on discharge documentation.The method centered on an approach that used a large language model (LLM) -- a form of AI that can process and generate text -- to develop discharge summaries for complex patient cases.Clinicians helped design the approach based on the information physicians need after patient discharge. The LLM process organised patient medical records and other information to create a patient summary that provided the core information for a patient discharge summary—all within a few minutes.The researchers at Stony Brook University compared LLM-generated and human-authored discharge summaries for 60 internal medicine hospitalisations at Stony Brook University Hospital lasting seven to 21 days, with paired assessment by hospitalists and primary care physicians.They found that the physician reviewers preferred the AI-generated discharge summaries in 95% of the evaluated hospitalisations. Additionally, the reviewers gave the summaries higher scores for overall quality, readability, accuracy and completeness. They also identified fewer missing clinical details compared to the human-authored summaries.According to the researchers, primary care physicians also found the AI-generated (LLM) summaries easier to understand, easier to explain to patients and caregivers, and more useful for follow-up care."These results provide evidence that artificial intelligence can support discharge documentation for complex hospital stays," said Rachel Wong, co-corresponding author and clinical associate professor at Stony Brook University.The team also found that both types of discharge summaries contained errors. Yet, physician reviewers found no statistically significant difference in the estimated severity or likelihood of harm associated with those errors. The authors stress that physician review and verification remain essential before any LLM-generated discharge draft is used for a patient record.
Article Summary: Discharge summaries provide essential information for patients when they leave a hospital. The data includes essential information such as a patient's treatment, medication needs, changes in medication, unresolved medical issues and follow-up needs. Primary care physicians rely on discharge summaries to continue their care of patients.

Article Title: Water dept to trace & tax farmers using canal-recharged water without paying user charges
Article Text:
File pic of canal

Nashik:





The water resources department has begun an exercise to identify farmers who use wells that are located in the vicinity of canals and irrigate cash crops without paying any charges for the water irrigation facility.WRD releases water through canals for agriculture based on farmers’ water demand, which is drawn for irrigation purposes and an irrigation charge is levied on the farmers for water.A senior engineer from the Nashik irrigation department said, “Cash crops like sugarcane, banana and cotton are being watered by drawing water from wells that are within the 35-meter zone along canals. This is unauthorised use and the department is identifying such farmers to charge them for irrigation facilities.”Generally, orchards are taken up by farmers where there is no constant water flow, and since these farmers are looking for a water source, they tap farmers who have agricultural land along canals.Farmers along water bodies sell off a small portion of their land to farmers with orchards to dig wells. The orchard owners then install water pumps and take the water to a far-off distance–even up to four km from the canal.“When water is released for irrigation purposes through canals, wells are recharged by water percolating through canal structures.This water is then pumped up for orchards far away. They pay no fee for this use, which is half the charge for flow irrigation. To locate such users, WRD has decided to launch a massive hunt for such farmers,” the officer added.WRD has ordered its personnel to identify the wells in the zones and establish their ownership. With the help of the revenue and land records department, the names of small plot owners will be identified, and their registrations will be checked for wells.“This way, we will be able to locate the well owners and their related farms based on which user charges will be levied,” the officer said.The officer added that the exercise will not only help in realising lost revenue but will also help identify the exact areas being cultivated through the respective irrigation projects. “This exercise will help us in truing up irrigated land across the state,” the officer added.
Article Summary: The water resources department has begun an exercise to identify farmers who use wells that are located in the vicinity of canals. The department is identifying such farmers to charge them for irrigation facilities.Generally, orchards are taken up by farmers where there is no constant water flow, and since these farmers are looking for a water source.

Article Title: Mother fights to save Leicester leisure centre pool as council considers closure, warning her severely disabled son could lose his only accessible swimming facility
Article Text:
PC: Wikipedia

What makes pool facilities essential for Susan Wilder’s son

Family struggles to find an accessible swimming pool for disabled son

New Parks closure plan sparks concern over disabled son's swimming access

How does the council plan to support swimmers with complex disabilities

A mother in Leicester is urging the city council to keep New Parks Leisure Centre open, warning that its closure could leave her severely disabled son without access to a suitable swimming pool. Susan Wilder, 67, said the centre was the only facility she had found that could accommodate her 19-year-old son, who uses a wheelchair full-time and has complex physical, visual and hearing impairments.According to the BBC, swimming provides him with his only form of cardiovascular exercise and gives him a sense of freedom. Leicester City Council is consulting on proposals to close the leisure centre and invest £8 million in transforming Leicester Leys Leisure Centre.Wilder said her son had been swimming at New Parks Leisure Centre for 19 years. He attends once one week and twice the next. She explained that he cannot use a standard pool chair because of his complex disabilities and requires specialist facilities to enter the water safely.He requires a poolside changing room with a ceiling-track hoist and a changing bed. The bed is brought to the poolside before he is transferred into the water using the hoist.Wilder said, "He loves the freedom of it and it's also the only cardiovascular exercise he gets.”"He has no speech, but he just generally loves the water."Wilder said her family had searched for alternative swimming facilities, including centres outside Leicestershire, but had been unable to find a suitable option for her son.Wilder said, "We're willing to travel with him, we're willing to travel out of the county, but there's nowhere available to meet his needs.”She explained that while many disabled people could use swimming pools with the help of a pool chair, her son's needs were different. He requires facilities that allow him to be transferred from his changing bed into the water using a ceiling-track hoist.She said, "You have to look at people's needs to be able to access a swimming pool in the correct way. It's not just for my son, it's for anybody that has the disabilities that he's got.”Leicester City Council has described New Parks as the city's least used leisure centre and plans to spend £8 million transforming Leicester Leys Leisure Centre under the proposals.A petition calling for New Parks to be saved has received more than 2,150 signatures. However, Wilder said Leicester Leys would be too busy for her son because of his multi-sensory impairment, which includes hearing and visual impairments. She said he would not be able to swim there even if a pool hoist were installed.Wilder also expressed concern that the future of New Parks might already have been decided.According to Leicester Mercury, she said, “It’s a dif­fer­ent feel­ing; it’s sens­ory and helps relax him. I just want to make the coun­cil under­stand how import­ant it is that he and oth­ers get access to be able to swim.”“This is why I’m so against New Parks clos­ing.”Leicester City Council said it had spoken to a range of swimming pool users during the consultation to understand their individual requirements and explore whether their needs could be met at other sites.A council spokesperson said, "All city council swimming pools offer disabled pool hoists designed to support users with diverse mobility requirements and transfer preferences, including compatibility with standard slings and adapted poolside chairs.”"After speaking with Sue, we understand that her son needs deeper water, so Aylestone Leisure Centre is making some small adaptions that will mean this centre will also be suitable for them and others to use.”"No decision has been made on the future of New Parks Leisure Centre, and we encourage everyone to have their say by November 3rd."
Article Summary: Leicester City Council is consulting on proposals to close New Parks Leisure Centre. Susan Wilder, 67, said the centre was the only facility she had found that could accommodate her 19-year-old son, who uses a wheelchair full-time. He requires a poolside changing room with a ceiling-track hoist and a changing bed.

Article Title: A couple bought a derelict Land Rover dealership for £330,000 and turned it into a five-bedroom home; the forecourt can fit around 50 cars
Article Text:
The couple have transformed this disused Land Rover dealership into a family home. Image Credit: Jam Press (@fearlessaliceblog)/Birmingham Mail

How did the couple turn a derelict Land Rover dealership into a 5-bedroom home

The couple: Niamh Coop and her husband Brandon. Image Credit: Birmingham Live

The upper floor now houses 5 bedrooms for family living

A forecourt large enough for around 50 cars remains part of the property

Image Credit: Forgotten Buildings/Supercar Blondie

The renovation could offer substantial savings compared with buying a larger home

A couple have given a disused Land Rover dealership in Derbyshire, England a new lease of life by transforming the former commercial property into a family home. Purchased for £330,000, the building had stood empty for more than a decade before its new owners began adapting it for residential use. The project has allowed them to make use of an existing structure rather than start from scratch, while the large forecourt remains one of the property's most unusual features, with enough room to accommodate around 50 cars.According to SupercarBlondie, the family bought the former dealership for £330,000 while it was still classified as a commercial property. The building had remained unused for more than 10 years, leaving its new owners with the challenge of turning a space designed for business into somewhere suitable for everyday family life.The purchase was not entirely straightforward. The property's commercial classification added extra legal and lending requirements, making the buying process more time-consuming than a typical residential purchase.Once the sale was completed, the couple could begin adapting the building. Rather than demolishing it and constructing a completely new house, they worked with the existing structure, removing much of the interior to create a layout that would function as a home.One of the most significant parts of the renovation was the redesign of the building's upper level. According to Supercar Blondie, the space has been rebuilt to include 5 bedrooms, giving the property the layout expected of a family home rather than a commercial premises.The change required more than simply moving furniture into an existing showroom. Much of the interior had to be removed to make room for a more practical arrangement. The aim was to create spaces that could be used comfortably for everyday activities, with separate bedrooms forming an important part of the new layout.The decision to retain the original structure also shaped the project. Instead of undertaking a complete rebuild, the owners adapted what was already there.The former dealership's forecourt is another distinctive feature of the converted home. According to the Birmingham Mail report, the outdoor space can accommodate around 50 cars, giving the property a large area for parking.For a typical family house, even a spacious driveway would rarely offer anything approaching this capacity. The forecourt reflects the building's original purpose, when space was needed to display vehicles and accommodate customers visiting the dealership.Although the property has changed its role, the expansive outdoor area remains an important part of its character. It also illustrates the difference between converting a commercial building and buying a house designed from the outset for residential use.A dealership requires a layout that supports business operations, including vehicle access and substantial external parking. A family home, by contrast, needs comfortable living areas and rooms suited to everyday routines. The couple's project brings these different requirements together on one site.The financial side of the project was another reason the conversion attracted attention. Supercar Blondie reported that the couple had spent around £90,000 on the renovation at the time of its report, with total spending expected to remain below £200,000.The reported figures suggest that adapting the property could be considerably less expensive than purchasing a comparable 5-bedroom home in the same area. Supercar Blondie stated that the family estimated savings of around £230,000 through the conversion.Renovation expenses can vary depending on the building's condition, the work required to make it suitable for living and the changes needed to create a practical layout. The dealership's commercial classification also meant the purchase involved additional legal and lending requirements.The transformation also reflects a broader opportunity to reuse buildings that are no longer required for their original purpose. Disused dealerships, with their substantial floor areas and open layouts, can offer possibilities beyond vehicle sales. Other abandoned dealerships have also been repurposed, although not all have been converted into homes.
Article Summary: A couple have converted a disused Land Rover dealership in Derbyshire, England into a 5-bedroom home. Purchased for £330,000, the building had stood empty for more than a decade before its new owners began adapting it for residential use. The renovation could offer substantial savings compared with buying a larger home.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung , Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.
Article Summary: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians. The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.

Article Title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags vulnerabilities
Article Text:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a criticalseverity warning. (Reuters photo)

CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities

BENGALURU: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems.Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual.

Article Title: Zomato launches Host Mode, lets users hide menu prices from guests: Here’s how it works
Article Text:
Designed to make hosting more comfortable

How Host Mode works

Feature inspired by customer feedback

Food delivery platform Zomato has launched a new feature called Host Mode, aimed at making group food ordering more comfortable by hiding menu prices from guests while allowing hosts to retain control over the final bill. The new feature, which is now available to users across India, enables guests to browse restaurant menus and add dishes to the cart without seeing the cost of individual items. Hosts can later review the complete bill and place the order after authenticating with a passcode, fingerprint, or face lock.According to Zomato, the feature addresses a common social situation where guests often hesitate to order their preferred dishes when someone else is paying. The company said many diners tend to choose less expensive items or leave the decision to the host, while hosts typically want their guests to order freely without worrying about the cost.With Host Mode enabled, prices are removed from restaurant menus and the cart, allowing guests to focus solely on choosing what they would like to eat. The total bill remains hidden until the host decides to exit the mode and review the order.The company said the feature is particularly relevant during the festive season, when families and friends frequently gather and order food together.Users can activate the feature by tapping the Host Mode option available on the app's home screen, restaurant menu pages, or through the preferences section in their profile.Once enabled, prices disappear across menus and the cart, and guests can add items without seeing any pricing information. When the order is ready, the host can tap the option to exit Host Mode, authenticate using biometric verification or device security credentials, and view the complete bill, including any discounts or savings, before placing the order.Zomato said only the host can reveal the bill, ensuring that pricing details remain private throughout the ordering process.The company revealed that Host Mode originated from a suggestion shared by a Zomato customer on social media. According to Zomato, the idea was developed and rolled out on the app within 72 hours, with the goal of making social hosting and food ordering more seamless for customers. The launch adds to Zomato's ongoing efforts to introduce features aimed at improving user experience on its food delivery platform, particularly around social and group ordering occasions.
Article Summary: Zomato has launched a new feature called Host Mode, aimed at making group food ordering more comfortable by hiding menu prices. The new feature, which is now available to users across India, enables guests to browse restaurant menus and add dishes to the cart without seeing the cost of individual items.

Article Title: Google launches Dreambeans AI app to India, brings personalised story collections in 14 languages
Article Text:
What is Google’s Dreambeans app

Uses data from Google's apps

Available in 14 Indian languages

Google has announced that its experimental AI-powered app—Dreambeans is now available in India. The Dreambeans app is available for all the users above 18 years of age across the country. The tech giant has also revealed that the app is developed by Google Labs and is available on both Android and iOS operating systems. “Starting today, Dreambeans, an experimental app from Google Labs that creates personalized daily story collections, is expanding to people in India (18+),” said Google in a blog post.As per Google, Dreambeans is designed to connect you with what matters without the endless scroll. The app can help users create personalised daily story collections on the basis of their interests and activities. “Dreambeans is designed to connect you with what matters without the endless scroll. This could be everything from places to explore, new arts & crafts, or a reminder of upcoming local events. You can dive deeper into any story to learn more, bookmark for later, or easily share with others to spark inspiration,” added Google.Google says that the app is designed to help people discover information that matters to them without having to endlessly scroll through feeds and content streams.Google said Dreambeans generates its personalised content using information from selected Google services that users choose to connect. These include Google Calendar, Gemini, Gmail, Google Photos, Google Search and YouTube. The company added that user feedback will help improve the quality and relevance of stories generated by the app over time“Dreambeans brews your stories using information from the Google apps you select, including Calendar, Gemini, Gmail, Photos, Search, and YouTube. Share your feedback to make your stories even better over time,” said Google.As part of its India rollout, Dreambeans is launching with support for 14 languages. These include Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Marathi, Tamil, Urdu, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia, Punjabi, Assamese and Nepali, among others. Google said the app is available for download starting today through both the Google Play Store and Apple's App Store
Article Summary: Google has announced that its experimental AI-powered app—Dreambeans is now available in India. The Dreambeans app is available for all the users above 18 years of age across the country. The tech giant has also revealed that the app is developed by Google Labs.

Article Title: Google Pay gets new shopping feature with virtual try-on: What is Discover Shop and how it works
Article Text:
What is Discover Shop

How can users access it on Google Pay

How do virtual try-on and image search work

Google Pay is testing a shopping feature in India. Named Discover Shop, the experience introduces a personalised fashion and lifestyle feed inside the payments app, combining product listings, YouTube videos, visual search and AI-powered virtual try-on. Google says the pilot is currently available to a limited number of users as it gathers feedback.Eligible users can browse recommendations based on their consented Google activity, upload an image to find similar products and preview how select clothing items might look on them. Product discovery takes place within Google Pay, while purchases are completed on merchants’ websites using the shopper’s preferred payment method. Access also requires a personal Google Account with Web & App Activity and Search Personalization enabled.Discover Shop gives users a dedicated space to explore fashion products and styling content tailored to their preferences. Google says the experience draws on its Shopping Graph, a continually updated collection of information covering more than 60 billion products.The feed combines shopping recommendations with YouTube videos.Users can open individual listings to view details such as colour, size and other available options.Google is also bringing visual search and virtual try-on into the experience, allowing users to explore products through images as well as browse their personalised feed.Users can check availability by updating Google Pay to the latest version and looking for the Discover or Discover Shop icon at the bottom of the screen.Those with access can open the tab to load their feed and select a product for more information. The feature requires users to be signed into a personal Google Account and have both Web & App Activity and Search Personalization switched on.Updating the app does not guarantee access, as the rollout remains limited to selected users in India.For supported products, users can open a listing and select Try it on, followed by Try on you, to see an AI-generated preview of how the item looks on them. Google says it also plans to introduce pre-generated daily looks for outfit suggestions. That addition is described as coming soon.To find similar styles, users can select Search and point the camera at an item. They can also upload a photograph to discover visually similar products across the web.When a shopper selects an item they want to buy, the experience directs them to the merchant’s website to complete the transaction. Google says shoppers can use their preferred payment method there.
Article Summary: Discover Shop gives users a dedicated space to explore fashion products and styling content tailored to their preferences. Google says the experience draws on its Shopping Graph, a continually updated collection of information covering more than 60 billion products. Users can open individual listings to view details such as colour, size and other available options.

Article Title: Hackers hit Nvidia’s cloud development platform: What the company said in notification sent to affected customers
Article Text:
Nvidia

What Nvidia told affected users: Read notification

We are writing to inform you that NVIDIA Corporation ("NVIDIA") has experienced a security incident that may affect the security of your data. NVIDIA is providing this notice to you with details of the incident, our response, and resources available to you to help protect your personal information from possible misuse.

What Happened?

Our incident investigation identified unauthorized activity affecting the NVIDIA Brev platform from October 4 through October 20, 2026. We acted to secure our systems and to determine the information potentially affected. Our analysis determined that your information from our Brev network may have been affected.

What Information Was Involved?

Our analysis determined that the following information was potentially exposed: the SSH key that Brev provisioned for your Brev-provisioned VM.

This SSH key has since been rotated, and your instances have been updated with the replacement key. At this time, we are unaware of improper use of these keys.

Nvidia has been hit by another cyberattack, this time targeting its Brev cloud development platform. According to a report, unauthorised activity occurred on the service between October 4 and October 20, prompting the company to send formal breach notifications to affected users warning that their account information may have been exposed. Citing the customer notice, Tom’s Hardware reported that Nvidia launched an internal investigation after spotting unidentified activity on the platform. The probe determined that malicious actors may have accessed data stored on Brev systems, specifically compromising Secure Shell (SSH) keys configured by the service.In its communication to users, Nvidia confirmed the security breach and outlined the immediate technical steps taken to protect developer systems, while also stating that it replaced the compromised SSH keys with new credentials. The company added that its team has found no evidence showing the exposed keys were improperly used.The breach at Nvidia arrives amid a broader series of security incidents aimed at AI infrastructure providers and developer cloud platforms. For example, on October 30, cybersecurity firm Wiz published a report detailing what it described as a “Black October” for AI developer services. The firm tracked security incidents across at least nine platforms throughout the month.
Article Summary: N Nvidia has been hit by another cyberattack, this time targeting its Brev cloud development platform. According to a report, unauthorised activity occurred on the service between October 4 and October 20, prompting the company to send formal breach notifications to affected users. The probe determined that malicious actors may have accessed data stored on Brev systems.

Article Text:
New TV, new sound or both: your Diwali home theatre list

Price:

Price:

Diwali is when most people go out and buy something new for their homes, and more often than not it is a new TV. For others it is a soundbar to complete a home theatre they have been building, a full sound system, or at times the entire setup in one go. This list has all of it: five TVs, five sound systems and a streaming device, 11 products in total, for you to pick from depending on whether your room needs a better picture, fuller sound or a smarter way to stream.Start with what bothers you most. If it is the screen, the TVs here come in sizes and styles to suit different rooms. If it is the sound, the options run from a soundbar system and a pair of powered speakers to full surround setups, one of which also plays music in other rooms. If the TV is fine but the experience feels slow, the streaming device is a small fix.You do not have to buy it all. Pick one piece, or put the whole setup together over time. Here is what each product offers, so you can decide what your living room needs.Rs 1,34,990Samsung’s Micro RGB technology uses individually controlled red, green and blue micro LEDs to manage light and colour. The company says this is designed to deliver vivid colours and detailed images across different types of content, and it presents the technology as a change in how colour is reproduced and how the picture is processed.The 55-inch R85H is a 4K smart TV from the 2026 range with AI-powered picture optimisation and intelligent sound features, in a slim body meant for contemporary living rooms. Glare Free technology, which reduces reflections, is available only on select models, and Vision AI features for picture optimisation and content experiences vary by model, so the exact feature set of a given unit is worth confirming before purchase.Rs 1,60,261The C6 uses LG’s alpha 11 AI Processor Gen3 with a Dual AI Engine, which controls the panel’s 8.3 million self-lit pixels. LG says the NPU is up to 5.6 times faster than before, with the CPU 50% faster and the GPU 70% stronger. A Brightness Booster feature lifts highlights, and the panel carries UL-verified Perfect Black and Perfect Color, with certification for 100% colour volume and fidelity. On the gaming side it supports up to 165Hz at 4K with G-Sync compatibility and FreeSync Premium, a 0.1ms response time, VESA-certified DSC, Nvidia GeForce Now and a Game Dashboard. webOS adds an AI Hub with Multi AI Search using Gemini and Copilot, plus AI Concierge and voice profiles. The set is 45.1mm deep without its stand, and the webOS Re:New programme promises up to five years of software upgrades.Rs 3,59,900The 7 II uses what Sony calls True RGB, where red, green and blue LEDs in the backlight are controlled independently. Sony says this combines the colour range of its QD-OLED TVs with the brightness of Mini LED, and X-Wide Angle Pro keeps colour and contrast steady from side seats. The XR Processor with AI handles 4K upscaling and fast motion, and the TV supports IMAX Enhanced, Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos. A subwoofer, rear speakers or both can connect directly to the TV through BRAVIA Theatre, without a soundbar. For gaming, it offers 4K at 120fps and PS5 features such as Auto HDR Tone Mapping, though VRR support varies by model. It runs Google TV and comes in sizes from 55 to 98 inches.The Vision 9 is the biggest Lumio TV yet, a 65-inch QD-MiniLED set from the 2026 range. Lumio has put much of its pitch into speed. It runs a MediaTek Pentonic 700 chip with 3GB of RAM, and the company says the TV boots in seconds. Storage is 64GB, which Lumio says is 50 per cent faster than before, so apps install and load quicker. A Wi-Fi chip is meant to keep streaming smooth. On the software side, the TV runs TLDR 2.0, Lumio’s own content discovery platform, which pulls together trending titles and recommendations across apps. The remote has a dedicated TLDR button to open it. Lumio is also offering a free third year of warranty on the 65-inch model, and its Diwali sale offers are live on the site.Rs 79,990Hisense’s U7SE is a 4K Mini LED TV, and the 55-inch is the smallest of four sizes that go up to 85 inches. It uses a Hi-QLED panel and a Total HDR solution for picture quality. Gamers get a native 144Hz mode, and a built-in subwoofer adds some bass without an extra box. It runs on VIDAA, Hisense’s own smart TV platform, and supports hands-free voice control. If you want a Mini LED screen and a larger size, the same series covers it.Rs 22,999The Aura 5 is a pair of powered speakers, not a soundbar. It uses 4.5-inch woofers and 1-inch silk dome tweeters in wooden enclosures, and the amplifier and DAC sit inside the right speaker, so no receiver is needed. That speaker also carries every input: HDMI ARC with CEC, optical, coaxial, USB, RCA/AUX and Bluetooth 5.4. Connect it to the TV over HDMI and the TV remote controls the volume. Lumio quotes a 35Hz to 20kHz response and lossless playback up to 24-bit/48kHz. The supplied cable between the two speakers is 2 metres, which sets how far apart they can sit unless you use your own wire.Rs 60,000Sonodyne has been making audio gear in India since 1970, and the SAMA 6000 is its 5.1-channel Dolby Atmos system. The soundbar carries five full-range drivers for the left, right, centre and side-firing surround channels. The wireless subwoofer has an 8-inch driver, and total output is 700W. One HDMI eARC cable connects it to the TV, and the subwoofer pairs automatically. HDMI in, optical, AUX and Bluetooth are also on offer. Three EQ modes cover movies, music and dialogue, the subwoofer level can be adjusted separately, and the system carries a two-year warranty.Rs 1,10,990The Q990H is an 11.1.4-channel system, meaning 11 front and surround channels, one subwoofer channel and four up-firing channels. The bar itself has front-firing, side-firing and up-firing speakers, and the box includes a subwoofer with dual 20.32 cm units and AI Dynamic Bass Control, plus two wireless rear speakers that can face front or back. Dolby Atmos is transmitted wirelessly over Wi-Fi with 2022 to 2026 Samsung TVs, and Eclipsa Audio is supported. Q-Symphony plays sound through the TV and soundbar together, SpaceFit Sound Pro tunes the output to the room, and Active Voice Amplifier Pro raises dialogue over background noise. Other features include Game Pro mode, Private Rear Sound for late-night viewing, HDMI 2.1 with eARC, Google Cast, AirPlay, Spotify Connect and SmartThings.Rs 1,83,997This set bundles four products: the Arc Ultra soundbar, the Sub 4 wireless subwoofer and two Era 100 smart speakers. Sonos describes it as plug and play, with setup done through the Sonos app once the products are powered on. The speakers can be mixed and matched, so the system can serve both the TV and music in other parts of the home, and more Sonos products can be added later. The Arc Ultra is priced at Rs 84,999 on its own, the Sub 4 at Rs 67,999 and each Era 100 at Rs 21,999. The retailer lists delivery within six to seven business days.Rs 2,39,990The Trio is Sony’s flagship wireless home theatre system, and it takes a different approach from a soundbar. Dedicated left, centre and right speakers are meant to create a wider soundstage than a single bar, and Sony says the layout is aimed at today’s very large TVs. It supports Dolby Atmos and DTS and integrates with compatible BRAVIA televisions. The figure of up to 24 phantom speakers applies when it is paired with the Sub 9 and Rear 9. The Sub 9 is a 600W subwoofer with dual opposing drivers, priced at Rs 94,990, and the Rear 9 has large up-firing speakers and a swivel wall-mount bracket, priced at Rs 74,990. Both are sold separately.Rs 39,900 (2026 model, pre-order); Rs 16,900 (2022 model)The Apple TV 4K is not a necessary addition to a home theatre, but it is a worthwhile one. It is a small streaming box that plugs into the HDMI port of any TV above and brings Apple TV, Apple Music, Apple Arcade and Photos to the screen, with 4K Dolby Vision, HDR10+ and Dolby Atmos in supported apps. The 2026 model swaps the 2022 model’s A15 chip for an A19, adds Wi-Fi 7 and a far-field microphone for Siri AI, and works as a smart home hub with HomeKit and Matter accessories. It is on pre-order from 13 November at Rs 39,900, more than twice the Rs 16,900 at which the 2022 model is listed at one retailer, and Apple says Siri AI also works on the second-generation box and later. If you want one this Diwali, the 2022 model is the one to look for, provided it costs less than the new one.
Article Summary: Diwali is when most people go out and buy something new for their homes. For others it is a soundbar to complete a home theatre they have been building, or a full sound system. This list has five TVs, five sound systems and a streaming device, 11 products in total.

Article Title: From turning first dates into interviews to using ChatGPT for replies and tracking matches in spreadsheets: How AI companies are changing San Francisco’s dating scene
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

When first dates become interviews

“You don’t need to understand if they have cancer in their family; you don’t need to understand on the first date if they really want three children,”

ChatGPT replies and spreadsheets for matches

Singles are trying alternatives to dating apps

San Francisco’s artificial intelligence (AI) boom is changing how some residents date. AI company founders and engineers working long hours are bringing their professional habits into their personal lives, screening potential partners against detailed criteria and approaching first meetings like interviews. According to a New York Times report, some also use ChatGPT to review messages and analyse their dating history, while others link dating-app data to spreadsheets to track matches.The report describes a dating scene shaped by limited free time and pressure to find a suitable partner quickly. A coach charging tech founders $5,000 a month frames dating in business metrics, while some workers struggle to fit meetings into demanding schedules. For those seeking relationships, the habits used to build a company can make getting to know someone feel like another work task.Mehul Agarwal, the 24-year-old co-founder of AI filmmaking startup Koyal, described one date that took two months to schedule. Both worked at AI startups and arrived exhausted. Their familiarity with professional small talk made the evening feel like a networking meeting.Agarwal wants to find a wife before becoming wealthy, so he will not have to question whether a partner is attracted to his success.But work and travel have limited his opportunities to build a relationship.Other daters described being assessed against a checklist. Amanda Chung, 25, who works at AI startup Nectar Social, said one founder could meet only after 10 p.m. Another asked about her job and work style.Sina Hartung, a co-founder of Eureka Health, asked how much some people expect to establish right away.she told NYT.Joyce Zhang, a former Stripe product manager who now coaches tech founders on dating, said some clients treat finding a partner as a problem money and optimisation can solve.She uses familiar business language, discussing their “top of funnel”, meaning the pool of potential partners, and the proportion of connections that become dates.Some clients link dating-app information to spreadsheets. Others focus on understanding the apps’ algorithms or run replies through ChatGPT. Some give the chatbot their entire dating history and ask it to identify patterns. Zhang said her coaching encourages clients to trust their intuition rather than rely entirely on analysis.Some residents are organising events that give people another way to meet. At Kilowatt, a bar in San Francisco’s Mission neighbourhood, participants at a “Date My Ex” event used short slide presentations to introduce potential partners to the audience.The event is part of a “Date My Friend” series organised by Annalise Wulf and two friends as an alternative to apps and a response to demanding dating criteria.Wulf said long startup hours leave little room for connections that develop gradually. Many AI startup workers follow a “996” schedule: 9 am to 9 pm, six days a week.
Article Summary: AI company founders and engineers working long hours are bringing their professional habits into their personal lives. They are screening potential partners against detailed criteria and approaching first meetings like interviews. Some also use ChatGPT to review messages and analyse their dating history. Others link dating-app data to spreadsheets to track matches.

Article Title: CEO of $300 billion cybersecurity company ‘warns’ of more hacking, shares 3 key points on what has changed and advice to companies
Article Text:
Nikesh Arora, CEO of Palo Alto Networks

What has changed: 3 key points behind the surge

Attacks will accelerate from here on - We are there: Six months ago I said

Mythos

like capability will be widely available. It's happening. A critical vulnerability, a social engineering attack that looks innocuous, or daisy chaining publicly available vulnerabilities and conducting a sniper strike is all being witnessed in the wild. Incident responders have never been busier.

Some key points:

- attacks are not becoming more sophisticated, it's the same attacks, faster and by a lot more people.

- attack path discovery which took trial and error and multiple attempts is now trivial, open source LLMs are here to help

- you are as secure as your supply chain, insecure down or upstream players who have access to your infrastructure could be the next attack path, marketplaces and supply chain is an easier vector

Nikesh Arora’s advice to companies

The increase in activity is a result of more people becoming better at hacking due to the ease of being able to attack.

Had not contemplated that in my calculus.

Please:

1. Test your infrastructure for accessible vulnerabilities and misconfigurations

2. Fix your code and demand your vendors do.

3. Old infra, or insecure infra at the perimeter needs to be updated first

4. New AI tools, especially coding need a security framework. Your developers will do more with code, new skills, and more automation. Don't forget the coding models have trained on human code.

Nikesh Arora, the CEO of $300 billion cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks, has sounded an alarm on a sharp increase in cyberattacks, warning that hacking incidents will accelerate rapidly from here on out. The top executive recounted that he sounded the alarm six months ago, highlighting that incident response teams will be busier than ever as high-level, AI-powered capabilities become widely available. Article Title: Apple CEO John Ternus takes a different approach to AI race, says for Apple what matters is…
Article Text:
Apple CEO John Ternus

Apple CEO rejects AI ‘agent’ takeover

Focus on security and privacy over regulation debates

As tech giants race to deploy artificial intelligence (AI) tools and autonomous agents across every layer of computing, Apple ’s new CEO John Ternus is taking a sharply different path. He took the helm of the company during a time of significant technological disruption in its 50-year history. Ternus made it clear that Apple will not chase AI simply for the sake of following industry trends. Instead, he argued that the real test is user experience, not the technology powering it behind the scenes.“Everyone has an opinion – I really like where we’re at,” Ternus said in an interview with Wired. He added: “I would hope people recognise that the work we do is building incredible products that make their lives better. We’re absolutely going to leverage AI to do that. We don't want to ship AI for AI's sake. When we're doing it right, people won’t have to think about whether it was AI that made this happen or more traditional software. What matters is, did we build something that they really love?”While rivals like Google , Microsoft, Meta and OpenAI pour resources into tools designed to write code, replace entire workflows, generate autonomous content and deploy independent agents that act without asking, another faction predicts AI will completely absorb the traditional app ecosystem.Ternus dismissed this narrative, pushed back on the idea of removing humans from the process.“That could make life really easy, I suppose, but the creation of products is a deeply human and personal thing, something that we love to do,” Ternus stated.The stance creates a visible contrast between Apple and the rest of Silicon Valley. While competitors push to automate workflows and substitute human labour with AI models, Ternus is drawing a line between pure automation and human craftsmanship, asserting that product creation still hinges on taste, judgment and human involvement.Addressing questions regarding AI regulation, Ternus steered the focus back toward device integrity, cybersecurity and protecting consumer privacy.“We all read the stories and think about it from a cybersecurity standpoint—clearly these models are very capable of doing things. Our focus is on making sure that our products are secure and safe, and protecting the users' information,” Ternus said.
Article Summary: Apple CEO John Ternus says the real test is user experience, not the technology powering it behind the scenes. The stance creates a visible contrast between Apple and the rest of Silicon Valley. While competitors push to automate workflows and substitute human labour with AI models, Ternu is drawing a line between pure automation and human craftsmanship.

Article Title: Apple HomeView's built-in camera may gain recording and motion detection features
Article Text:
Apple's Next HomeView Could Swivel a 9-Inch Screen on a Robotic Arm to Face You

Hidden code points to security camera mode

HomeView already includes a built-in camera

Privacy-focused features reportedly in development

Apple yet to confirm feature

Apple’s new HomeView smart display may be able to act as a home security camera, according to references found in its software, The Verge reports. A Reddit user spotted the feature in the settings files of HomeView Software 27.2. Apple has not announced anything about it, and Digital Trends notes that the feature is not active in the current software.The HomeView is Apple’s recently unveiled smart home display. It already has a built-in camera for FaceTime calls and facial recognition. The camera is a 12MP unit that can recognise people on sight, which matters in a home shared by a whole family. The settings files suggest Apple could also use the same hardware for motion detection, live streaming and video recording through HomeKit Secure Video.According to a report by The Verge, Reddit user "pdfu" uncovered references within HomeView software version 27.2 that describe a dedicated security camera mode. The code strings mention motion detection, live streaming, video recording options, and several privacy-focused features. One setup screen reportedly states: "Your HomeView can be used as a security camera with HomeKit Secure Video." The discovery suggests that Apple may be planning to leverage the HomeView's built-in camera for home monitoring purposes, although the company has not officially announced such a feature.Apple unveiled the HomeView smart display at its "Welcome Home" event in October 2026. The device features a 7-inch display and a 12-megapixel camera designed for FaceTime calls and facial recognition. The camera can recognise multiple users and personalise content based on who is standing in front of the device. The HomeView currently serves as a central smart home control hub, allowing users to manage connected devices, view feeds from security cameras and access Siri-powered smart home features.The leaked code strings indicate that Apple is building several privacy protections into the potential security camera mode. According to the report, video feeds would only be viewable by members of the household, while the device would display a visual indicator and play a sound whenever someone starts watching the camera feed or when recording begins. Household members would also reportedly receive notifications whenever security camera settings are changed. The software code further points to configurable settings that would allow users to determine what the camera should detect, stream or record depending on whether they are at home, away or asleep.While the code references strongly hint at upcoming functionality, Apple has not publicly confirmed plans to turn HomeView into a security camera. The Verge noted that the company may still be refining privacy safeguards before rolling out such a feature, given Apple's longstanding emphasis on user privacy and security. If introduced, the feature would further expand HomeView's role within Apple's growing smart home ecosystem and could make the device a more direct competitor to smart displays from rivals that already offer integrated home monitoring capabilities.
Article Summary: Hidden code points to security camera mode on Apple's HomeView smart display. HomeView already includes a built-in camera for FaceTime calls and facial recognition. Code strings mention motion detection, live streaming, video recording options, and several privacy-focused features. Apple yet to confirm feature.

Article Title: Godfather of AI Geoffrey Hinton says Google will win the AI race; those less likely to win are Microsoft and …
Article Text:
Godfather of AI Geoffrey Hinton

Geoffrey Hinton says Microsoft and Meta are less likely to win AI race

Why Geoffrey Hinton favours Google

Godfather of AI Geoffrey Hinton believes tech giant Google has a strong chance of winning the AI race, while Microsoft and Meta may be less likely to emerge as leaders. However, Hinton also acknowledged that his past association with Google could influence his view. "If I had to bet on one lot of people, it would probably be Google," Geoffrey Hinton said while sharing his views on which companies could lead the AI race. "But I used to work for Google, so don't take me too seriously about that. I have a vested interest in them winning," he further added.Hinton, who is widely known as the 'Godfather of AI' for his pioneering work in the field, also named Anthropic and OpenAI as companies that could challenge Google.While Geoffrey Hinton sees Google as a likely contender, he believes Microsoft and Meta have a lower chance of winning the AI race."Anthropic might win. OpenAI might win," he said. "I think it's less likely that Microsoft will win or that Facebook will win," Hinton added.Geoffrey Hinton also explained that the outcome may depend less on who leads a company and more on its ability to attract talented people and provide them with the resources needed to develop AI."It's not who's running it, it's who has the resources to get the right people to do the work."Geoffrey Hinton's comments come with an important qualification. He previously worked at Google, where he spent more than a decade researching artificial intelligence before leaving the company in 2023. He spent about 10 years working on artificial neural networks and deep learning technologies for Google. In 2012, his work (alongside his students) on AlexNet laid the technical foundation for modern generative AI and large language models.After leaving Google, Hinton was awarded the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics for his foundational discoveries and inventions in machine learning with artificial neural networks.
Article Summary: Godfather of AI Geoffrey Hinton believes tech giant Google has a strong chance of winning the AI race. Hinton also named Anthropic and OpenAI as companies that could challenge Google. He previously worked at Google, where he spent more than a decade researching artificial intelligence before leaving in 2023.

What users should do

Don't click links in unexpected emails claiming to come from Bandai Namco or The GUNDAM base. Check the sender address closely before opening anything. If you reuse a password across accounts, change it as a precaution, although passwords weren't part of this leak. Consider using a unique email alias for gaming accounts.

Bandai Namco, the publisher behindand a long list of other popular games, has confirmed a data breach that exposed customer information. The company wasn't hacked directly, and the problem came from a third-party email service provider called YmirLink.YmirLink's systems were compromised in a much larger leak, resulting in Bandai Namco's details also being leaked. In the section below, we take a detailed look at the Bandai Namco data breach.Bandai Namco says the breach exposed the data of roughly 346,000 members of The GUNDAM base, its Gundam-focused membership service. The company announced the incident on October 28, 2026. The notice has since been taken down from its site.The root cause lies with YmirLink, which handles email distribution for multiple organizations. Bandai Namco is one of several customers affected, so the incident is an example of supply-chain risk: a breach at a vendor spreads to every company relying on it.The exposure is limited, which is the good news. According to Bandai Namco, the leaked information includes only:The company says the following were not leaked:This sets the incident apart from Sony's recent So-net and plala breach, where names, phone numbers, and some bank account records were exposed.The Bandai Namco numbers are a small piece of a much bigger problem. Japanese broadcaster NHK reports that YmirLink first disclosed about 9 million leaked records on October 19. Further investigation raised the total to more than 51.62 million records. The data is mostly email addresses, and it affects other organizations that use YmirLink. Japanese railway operators JR Central, JR West, and JR Kyushu have also reported possible leaks.The company has taken several steps:Bandai Namco says it hasn't confirmed any secondary damage, such as misuse of personal information, as of its announcement.Even without passwords or payment details, exposed email addresses carry risk. Attackers can use them for phishing or impersonation, particularly if they can pair the address with an internal ID that looks official. Bandai Namco has warned affected users to be careful with suspicious messages. It added that any emails it sends about the incident will not contain URLs in the body, so a message about this breach that includes a link should be treated as a red flag.The investigation is ongoing, so the count could still change. The breach also follows Capcom's disclosure last week and Sony's earlier this week, which makes for a rough stretch for the gaming industry's data security. For now, the practical advice is simple: stay alert and don't trust links in unsolicited emails.
Article Summary: Bandai Namco has confirmed a data breach that exposed customer information. The company wasn't hacked directly, and the problem came from a third-party email service provider. The root cause lies with YmirLink, which handles email distribution for multiple organizations. The breach exposed the data of roughly 346,000 members of The GUNDAM base.

Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal
Article Text:
Formula E and Comsol

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development. It will introduce what Formula E describes as its fastest and most technologically advanced race car so far.COMSOL has also announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, which is scheduled to arrive later this autumn.The new version will include features aimed at advanced engineering work, including dedicated electric motor modelling, system-level simulation, agentic modelling and wider access to tools for creating simulation apps.The partnership was announced at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston. Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier also delivered a keynote speech at the event, discussing the technology and engineering that could shape the future of Formula E.
Article Summary: Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology. Aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process. AI and digital twins also in focus as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.
